description: Lag om forbud mot kop av sexuella tjanster (Sexkopslagen): purchase of sexual services criminalised, sale remains legal. First 'Nordic model' law.
Wet opheffing bordeelverbod: the 1912 general ban on brothels lifted; licensed sex businesses become legal and regulated.
Prostitutionsgesetz (ProstG): prostitution contracts made legally enforceable, procuring in licensed premises decriminalised.
Prostitution Reform Act 2003 (passed 60-59 on 25 June 2003): full decriminalisation of sex work, brothels licensed under ordinary law.
Act on the Punishment of Acts of Arranging Sexual Traffic and Act on the Prevention of Sexual Traffic: purchase and brokerage criminalised, red-light districts closed.
Purchase of sexual services criminalised (including by Norwegian nationals abroad).
Purchase of sexual services criminalised.
Policing and Crime Act 2009 s.14: strict-liability offence of paying for the sexual services of a prostitute subjected to force/exploitation (England and Wales).
Protection of Communities and Exploited Persons Act (PCEPA) in force; purchasing sex criminalised for the first time in Canada, after Bedford (20 Dec 2013) struck down the previous regime.
Loi n. 2016-444 du 13 avril 2016: purchase of sexual services penalised (fine up to EUR 1500), soliciting offence abolished.
Criminal Law (Sexual Offences) Act 2017 Part 4: purchase of sexual services criminalised.
Prostituiertenschutzgesetz (ProstSchG): compulsory registration of sex workers, licensing of premises, condom requirement.

Law Prohibiting the Consumption of Prostitution (Temporary Provision and Legislative Amendment) 5779-2019: adopted 31 Dec 2018, published 10 Jan 2019, in force 10 July 2020; made permanent in 2025. No post-reform years inside the 1960-2020 window.

description: Sex work decriminalised in the reformed Penal Code; first European country to do so. Outside the 1960-2020 estimation window.
Human Trafficking and Exploitation (Criminal Justice and Support for Victims) Act (NI) 2015 s.15, inserting Art 64A: purchase of sexual services criminalised. Rest of the UK unaffected.
A 2003 District Court ruling exposed a 1980 drafting error that had removed indoor prostitution from the statute; indoor sex work de facto decriminalised.
Indoor prostitution re-criminalised, closing the 1980 loophole.
Prostitution removed from the penal code's vagrancy provisions: selling sex becomes a lawful occupation (procuring and brothel-keeping stay illegal).
Act LXXV of 1999 on organised crime, Art. 8: municipalities may designate tolerance zones in which prostitution is permitted; sex work becomes a taxed, registered activity.
Law 2734/1999: prostitution permitted only in state-licensed brothels, with registration and health certification.
